correctness.rationale: Every derivation is D_(B,f); pair constraints at v and v+z force the central block difference to preserve all decomposable bivector lines and therefore be scalar. The Darboux projection lemma constructs a center dilation witness for arbitrary dependent-quotient pairs, and the half-identity derivation handles two central inputs in odd characteristic. Independent actual-path finite-field witness and linear-space-rank checkers passed; finite tests supplement, not replace, the unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: Searches of both the exact linear-two-local classification and equivalent exterior-square/derivation-reflexivity formulations did not locate a theorem covering all free two-step nilpotent Lie algebras of arbitrary generator rank at least three over odd-characteristic fields. The 2015 and 2024/2026 full texts support existence or related automorphism formulas, not the complete one-dimensional two-local defect. The 2015 general two-local paper could not be read in full; residual historical-priority risk is named, so this is a best-knowledge judgment, not a proof of absolute novelty.
residual_risks: The 2015 general two-local derivations paper was abstract-only; a stronger hidden statement or implication is possible.
Other algebraic-reflexivity/linear-2-local literature may use alternative terminology; semantic-index and web nonmatches are not a novelty proof.
Rank-two Heisenberg case is previously classified and excluded from novelty; the contribution is the uniform classification for all ranks at least three.

value.rationale: Complete rank-uniform classification of a natural linear two-point reflexive hull for all free class-two nilpotent Lie algebras in odd characteristic; it identifies an exact one-dimensional defect, proves a strict local/2-local/global hierarchy, and determines the 18/19/27 dimensional stratification in generator rank three. Broader structural motivation is independent of finite computations, and no general local-space classification in higher ranks is claimed.
